name: Cartouche
subtitle: Cartouche itself
description: The source Cartouche's built-in SideStore reads for Cartouche's own updates. It lists Cartouche and nothing else: Cartouche never lists, hosts or downloads games.

apps.name: Cartouche
apps.subtitle: Play your own games built with nxnative
apps.localizedDescription: Cartouche runs the games you build with nxnative from your own copies, renews itself without a computer, and gives them Increased Memory Limit. It never downloads a game.

versions.localizedDescription:
Cartouche 0.17.0 adds mods for each game, keeps your music playing, pauses a game when its controller disconnects, lets your Mac renew Cartouche and carries every profile of a game with its saves.

- Mods: on a game's sheet, Mods adds one from Files, as its folder or its ZIP, turns each on or off and sets their order, the one higher up winning. A mod that changes the game's code too is left out, with why. On your iPhone, iPad and Mac. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Home filter: with games installed and games not installed yet, on your Mac, in a games folder or in Cartouche Cloud, a menu beside My library shows All, Installed or Not installed, and L and R change it with a controller. Cartouche keeps your choice. Also on your Mac. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Saves folder: once your first game is over, while its saves are on this iPhone alone, the home offers to keep them safe in a folder on iCloud Drive, your Mac or a NAS: a tap opens Storage, and its × takes it off for good. A reinstall then loses nothing. Also on your Mac. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Your music while playing: turn on Keep other apps’ sound, in System › While a game runs, and the music or podcast you play in another app goes on under the game's sound, from the game's next start. Off until you turn it on. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Controller lost: a game pauses when its last controller disconnects. 3 seconds later the console comes back and says so, and connecting a controller again brings the game back. A game you play on the screen alone never pauses; System › While a game runs turns it off. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Renewed by your Mac: signed in once on the iPhone page of Cartouche for Mac, your Mac renews Cartouche on your iPhone in its last two days, by the cable or on your Wi-Fi, with no reinstall, and Cartouche shows its new date. Your password goes to Apple alone, and is asked again only once Apple ends the session. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Reinstalled by your Mac: when Cartouche's certificate is gone from your Apple Account, your Mac installs the newest Cartouche over it, with its games and saves: by itself once it expires, or at once with Reinstall on the iPhone page of Cartouche for Mac. It never revokes a certificate. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Every profile and shader: the saves of a game's players 2 to 8 now go and come with the first's, on your iPhone, iPad and Mac, each with the room the game made for it. A save from JKSV keeps the room it had on your console. And the shaders a game prepared come back after a reinstall, a reset or on another device, with those your other devices prepared, so its first games stutter less. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Back to the start: Put back a copy, on a game's sheet, now also lists the copies the game keeps on this iPhone of the saves each session starts from, even without a saves folder. If a game or a mod went wrong, put back the copy of its start; the saves it replaces are kept too. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Settings in your language: every setting nxnative gives a game now reads in your language, Rotation, Texture filtering and Microphone among them. Rotation now locks a game sideways or upright behind Cartouche's console too, as soon as you pick it in the game's menu. A game that has Polish or Thai starts in it on an iPhone set to it. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Prompts in your language: the prompt that waits for more players and the four labels of nxnative's menu over a game now read in Cartouche's language on your iPhone too, as on the Mac, behind the console or in Cartouche's place. The settings in that menu keep nxnative's English names. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Out of room: when a game stops because your iPhone ran out of room for the memory it keeps in files while it plays, Cartouche now says so and how much was free, instead of only saying the game closed. Before a start that may end that way, it warns you, with Play anyway. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Pipelines for your GPU: Cartouche now tells your Mac your iPhone's GPU, so that a game that bundles its Metal 4 pipelines, such as Breath of the Wild, is built with them for your iPhone too and no longer prepares them for minutes at its first start. Needs Cartouche for Mac 0.9.0, and a new build of the game. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Converted builds: on an iPhone whose GPU reads no BC textures, the question before an install now reads the game's build first: a build that converts its textures, from your Mac, a games folder or Cartouche Cloud, installs at once, and a Cartouche Cloud game built from nxnative-nobc says so on its sheet. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- iPhone 11 to 15: on an iPhone whose GPU reads no BC textures, the question before an install and System now say that Cartouche Cloud builds its games from nxnative-nobc too, for a game you send for an iPhone 11 to 15. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- LocalDevVPN port: signing in, renewing and updating no longer stop at once when another service of your iPhone answers at the port Cartouche reaches it at through LocalDevVPN: Cartouche looks for the right port again. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Certificate import: Import signing certificate opens the same Files picker as Import my copy, for the certificate (.p12) and its profile, so that the certificate you tap there comes back to the page, on iOS 27.3 too. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Install screen: while a game installs from your Mac on Wi-Fi, its screen no longer says cable because your iPhone was plugged in to the Mac for something else.

Cartouche 0.16.2 can bring a game of your NAS through your Mac and its cable, when the Mac is on Ethernet.

- NAS through your Mac: with the iPhone plugged into your Mac by a cable, and the Mac on Ethernet, the Mac reads the game on the NAS and passes it on through the cable, instead of the iPhone's Wi-Fi, and the install screen says By cable, through the Mac. On the Mac's Wi-Fi, the iPhone reads the NAS itself, as before. Needs Cartouche 0.8.1 or later on your Mac, which updates itself. Not tried with a real Mac and NAS yet.

Cartouche 0.16.1 installs again from your own SideStore: it asks your SideStore for the pairing file, and a copy without its app group says what to do.

- Your own SideStore: in 0.16.0, Cartouche asked its own built-in SideStore for the pairing file instead of yours; it asks yours again. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Without its app group: a copy of the IPA for SideStore installed without its app group, as some signing apps do, no longer asks for your Apple ID only to fail; it says so, and offers the IPA for your own certificate or the Installer instead. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.

Cartouche 0.16.0 speaks Spanish and German, installs from your own SideStore without a computer, guides you through the nightly renewal, reads several games folders, reaches your Mac by cable and sends your saves while you play.

- Spanish and German: Cartouche now speaks Spanish and German besides English and French, on the iPhone, the iPad and the Mac, and follows your device's language as before. The guides stay in English and French. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Your own SideStore: you can now install Cartouche with the SideStore you already have, no computer needed. Add the source source.cartouche.cloud to your SideStore and install Cartouche from it, keeping its extensions on the main profile. Its setup asks your SideStore for the pairing file, takes its certificate when you sign in with the same Apple ID, then reinstalls Cartouche once to get Increased Memory Limit. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Renew every night: the setup's last step guides you through the Shortcuts automation that renews Cartouche every night, and Cartouche now sees each of its runs: the step and System say whether it is to make, on, failed (no LocalDevVPN, interrupted, or SideStore's error) or no longer running. Once your first game is installed, the home reminds you of it until you make it or take the reminder off, and Cartouche asks to warn you before its signature expires. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Expired Apple session: when Apple says the session Cartouche renews with has expired, Cartouche signs in again by itself once and renews itself; otherwise the System page asks you to sign in again, and Cartouche no longer retries every six hours. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Your first game: with no game yet, How to get a game, beside Import my copy on the home and on a game's sheet, opens the guide. With no Mac, its third step now offers Cartouche Cloud, which builds your game for you, and I have my own IPAs already, which opens Files; linked to Cartouche Cloud, its last step installs the game it built, and the guide opens on the step left. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Several games folders: in Storage, Add another games folder reads another folder too, on any of your servers. A game in several shows once and installs from a folder whose server answers, so a game on your NAS that your Google Drive also holds installs away from home; its sheet says where the other copies are, and an install whose server does not answer goes on from the next copy. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Folders from the Mac: the games folders and the saves folder can now be changed on your Mac's console too, on one of your connections, and your iPhone takes them the next time Cartouche opens, the folder chosen last winning on either side. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Mac by cable: plugged into your Mac with a cable, the iPhone reaches Cartouche on your Mac and installs your games from it without Wi-Fi; Wi-Fi takes over again once unplugged. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Install speed: while a game installs from your Mac or a NAS, its screen shows how it comes (cable, Tailscale, or the Mac's Wi-Fi band) and how fast, with a tip when the Mac is on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi or the game comes slowly. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Saves sent while playing: a game behind the console sends its saves to your saves folder a few seconds after each save, not only after the game; offline, they still go after it. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- iCloud backup: the games Cartouche installs no longer go into your iPhone's backup, iCloud's or a computer's, as they install again from your storage; their saves still do. Games already installed leave it the first time this version opens. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Other installed apps: an IPA you install that is not an nxnative game is now on the System page, under Other installed apps, to open or uninstall; Cartouche no longer sends you to an Apps tab that does not exist. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- iPhones without BC: on an iPhone whose GPU reads no BC textures (iPhone 11 to 15), System and the question before an install now say that Cartouche on your Mac builds its games from nxnative-nobc, a separate fork of nxnative that converts those textures, once the two are paired. A game drawn with Vulkan whose build converts them is no longer Not supported on this iPhone, and a converted game still on your Mac or in a games folder no longer shows the warning before its install: its sheet says Textures converted for this GPU by this game's build. Games drawn with OpenGL keep the warning. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Game sheet memory: with Keep Cartouche open behind the game off, a game's sheet now counts the 8 GB Game Mode gives Cartouche a moment after it opens, on iPhones with 12 GB. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Cartouche Cloud games: a game you built and already installed now says On this iPhone instead of Install, and the Cloud page shows each game's cover and the four phases of its build as it runs. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Cartouche on the Mac: the Mac's app is now called Cartouche, as on the iPhone, and the Storage page says Add your Mac.

Cartouche 0.15.1 restores Apple Account sign-in.

- Cartouche uses the client format Apple expects for new sign-ins. This fixes the HTTP 503 at the start of sign-in.
- If you couldn’t sign in to update Cartouche, install this version over your current copy with Cartouche Installer 0.2.3. Your games and saves stay on the iPhone.
- A game’s sheet shows results for your device model first, with the newest results first in each group. The genre gets its own line when space is tight.

Cartouche now installs the games Cartouche Cloud builds for you without a Mac, no longer says Not supported on this iPhone of a game whose build converts its textures for your iPhone's GPU, and says in its own words what Apple answers when a sign-in does not go through.

- Cartouche Cloud: no Mac? Cartouche Cloud now builds your games for you, from the copy you send it on its site. In System › Cartouche Cloud, link Cartouche to your account with a code, follow each build, then install the games built, as from your games folder. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Game sheets: four more games have theirs, made from what players measured: Final Fantasy Resonance, Link's Awakening, Mario vs. Donkey Kong and Pokopia, which now shows On iPhone. The other sheets count the sessions played since. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Game sheets: on an iPhone whose GPU reads no BC textures, with an A16 chip or older, a game whose build converts them to ASTC, as a fork of nxnative does, is no longer Not supported on this iPhone: its sheet says Textures converted to ASTC by this game's build, and how it fits is decided as on other iPhones, by iOS, Increased Memory Limit, its memory and its results. A build that does not convert them, and a game drawn with Vulkan or OpenGL, keep the warning. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Signing in: when Apple refuses for now to set up a new sign-in on your iPhone, Cartouche now asks it once instead of once for each anisette server, says so in your language and has you wait before trying again, as after Apple's limits. When Apple says the sign-in has expired (1100), or refuses it without saying why (-22405), Cartouche now says what to do in your language too. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- TV mode: when the TV shows only the game's card, Report a problem now says whether the game's picture was there, and which nxnative built the game. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.

Cartouche now reaches your Mac and NAS away from home with Tailscale, your iPhone and your Mac share their storage connections and folders, and each copy of a game's saves names the version of the game that wrote it.

- Tailscale: installed apart on this iPhone and on your Mac or NAS, it lets Cartouche reach them away from home, your Mac by itself and a NAS by its name or address in Tailscale, and a Mac never met on your Wi-Fi pairs under Add your Mac › By its address. Storage › Away from home says whether it is connected. While it is on, Cartouche renews itself alone only in its last 2 days, as LocalDevVPN turns Tailscale off, and tells you when to turn it on again. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Game sheets: eight more games have theirs, made from what players measured: Super Mario Bros. Wonder, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, Pokémon Legends: Z-A, Ocarina of Time, Donkey Kong Bananza and Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave. Their page says whether your iPhone has what the game needs, and how it ran on iPhones like yours, and Cartouche starts each game where its memory fits. A game's title keeps its lines and its size on its page. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Storage: the Mac you pair with Cartouche Builder now keeps the same connections as this iPhone, passwords included, through the bridge's encryption: one you add, change or remove on either comes to the other. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Mac: when the saves folder or the games folder you chose is on one of your connections, your Mac with Cartouche Builder now keeps its games' saves in that saves folder, and sends its games to that games folder. Not tried on a real Mac yet.
- Mac: Cartouche Builder 0.7.0, which updates itself from 0.6.0 or 0.6.1, builds Mario Kart World again and gives Cartouche's console on your Mac a game's settings and saves on its sheet, and the System page as on your iPhone, with Your first game, Storage, Game measurements and Report a problem. Not tried on a real Mac yet.
- Builds: each build on your Mac now says what it is for, the iPhone, the Mac or both, on the game's sheet and in System › Builds, and a game whose app for the Mac alone is left to build says so, with Build its app for the Mac. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Saves: each copy of a game's saves now names the version of the game that wrote it, and an older version of the game never takes it: the game's sheet says the copy comes once the game is updated, and the saves played meanwhile go to your saves folder as a copy of their own. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Storage: How to name your games, under the games folder, shows with made-up examples what Cartouche finds in your games folder and your saves folder, and what Cartouche Builder finds in its dumps folder, each name found or left aside, and why. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Controllers: a controller now plays the game you start with Play. A game started that way got nothing from the controller, though it drove the console and hid the game's touch controls. Not tried on a real iPhone or iPad yet.
- After you free room by uninstalling games, an install is no longer refused with the room your iPhone had before, as Cartouche now reads the room again for each install.
- With your own certificate, when the certificate you choose does not go in, Cartouche now says why, such as a profile or a .zip chosen in its place, a password that does not open it, a .p12 without its private key, or, signed on your iPhone, a Cartouche to sign again in your signing app. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- When the part of Cartouche the built-in SideStore runs in (LiveProcess) is missing from your copy, a sign-in, a renewal or an update now says to install Cartouche again over itself with the Cartouche Installer, on your computer, with the same Apple ID, which puts it back and keeps your games and saves, instead of a message that sent you to other tools. Until then Cartouche no longer renews itself, and System says so under Renew now. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Reset Cartouche now empties the folder iOS keeps for what other apps open Cartouche with, instead of stopping on it, and goes through to the end. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Your first game: the link it sends your Mac now opens Cartouche Builder's page at cartouche.cloud, Cartouche's own address.
- Reports now also keep whole the From and To lines of an install from your games folder or a copy to it, and the journal's lines on saves and on Reset Cartouche, when your user name or a name in your storage settings is one of their words, such as games.
- Game settings: Press a button to join, Match screen for the picture shape, and the new note under Dynamic resolution now show in French too.

Cartouche 0.13.1 brings the fixes made since 0.13.0, and its update gives the games behind the console their full memory back.

- Memory: updated from 0.13.0 inside Cartouche, a copy that had lost Increased Memory Limit at an earlier update, about 3 GB for a game behind the console, gets it back, as 0.13.0 no longer signs the games' process without it. Games then start behind the console again, with the Home button, but for those that need more, such as Mario Kart World, which start in Cartouche's place. From 0.12.1 or older, the update after this one brings it back. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Renewal: when Apple revoked the certificate Cartouche is signed with, most likely because another app or computer took a new one with the same Apple ID, Cartouche now says to install it again over itself with the Cartouche Installer, on your computer, with the same Apple ID, which keeps your games and saves. Until then it no longer renews itself on that signature, and System says so under Renew now. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- When a renewal or an update could not reach your iPhone, Cartouche now says what to do, as the sign-in does: connect LocalDevVPN, join a Wi-Fi network, or put the pairing file in Cartouche again. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Signing in: if your Apple ID already has a certificate made by another app or computer, Cartouche now says so in your language, with what to do: sign in with the Apple ID you installed Cartouche with, if it was another, or else install Cartouche again over your copy with the Cartouche Installer and this Apple ID. Until now it showed English words that did not mention the Apple ID. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Signing apps: if signing in still stops on a copy that a signing app signed, its error now says what the setup says, and offers to download the same version's IPA for your own certificate, instead of "App Group Container Inaccessible". Not tried with a signing app or on a real iPhone yet.
- Reports, and the game logs you send to Cartouche, keep their Storage line whole when your user name or a name in your storage settings is one of its words, such as games: that word is no longer taken out as if it were yours.
- Cartouche Builder: when the app on your Mac is 0.5.0 or older, too old to update itself, a game's sheet and System › Builds on your Mac now say to download it once more, instead of to update it, and Send the link to your Mac sends it the link by AirDrop, Messages or Mail. It updates itself after that. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.

Cartouche now renews itself and connects LocalDevVPN by itself, your Switch games continue on your iPhone, Siri starts your games, and your Mac plays them with your iPhone's saves.

- Renewal: each time you open Cartouche in the last 3 days of its signature, it now renews itself as Renew now does, without you. System shows it under way, and why it failed, with its report; it tries again 6 hours later. Until now only Renew now, a Shortcuts automation or an update renewed Cartouche, whatever System said. A renewal keeps Increased Memory Limit.
- LocalDevVPN connects by itself: Renew now, Cartouche's own renewal, an update and the sign-in open LocalDevVPN, which connects and brings you back to Cartouche a second later. You no longer connect it first, nor leave it on all day. The first time, iOS asks you to allow LocalDevVPN's VPN configuration. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Renew every night: its steps in System now add LocalDevVPN's Enable LocalDevVPN action before Cartouche's Refresh All Apps, which waits for LocalDevVPN to connect. If you made this automation before, add that action before Refresh All Apps, or keep LocalDevVPN on.
- Renewal: an update or a sign-in started during a renewal waits for it to end, instead of failing with "Another refresh task is in progress". Renew now waits until Cartouche is set up.
- Continue on your iPhone a game you play on your Switch: export its save with JKSV or Checkpoint, put the folder or the ZIP in Files, then in the game's sheet choose Saves › Switch saves › Choose the exported save. Cartouche checks that it is this game's save and keeps the one it replaces, which you can put back. It works before the game's first start too.
- The other way, Make the ZIP for JKSV gives a ZIP of the game's save that JKSV restores on your Switch. Not yet tried with a real Switch save.
- Start a game with Siri or from your Home Screen: say "Play Mario Kart World in Cartouche", or use Cartouche's Play a Game action in the Shortcuts app and add that shortcut to your Home Screen as the game's own icon. A game's sheet shows how, under Siri and Home Screen. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- On an iPhone, games nxnative built since November 4 now turn upright as you hold your iPhone, their picture above their controls, as on the iPhone Duo's inner display: behind the console, and when they start in Cartouche's place. While the picture is on a TV, the iPhone stays sideways. Games built before stay sideways. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- The Home button over a game fades away a few seconds after the game shows: touch its place at the bottom of the screen to bring it back, then touch it again for the console.
- Games behind the console keep their full memory after Cartouche updates itself: an update no longer signs the games' process without Increased Memory Limit, which left some games about 3 GB there. A copy that already lost it gets it back at the update after this one, or at once by installing Cartouche again with the Cartouche Installer.
- Breath of the Wild, and any game that bundles a Metal pipeline archive for Apple's GPU, now installs signed whole: Cartouche signs only the files iOS loads code from. A game that still did not sign whole, or that stopped on an error as it started, now says why, with Sign again and play when that may help, instead of closing with nothing said. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Share a game's log from its sheet, under Share the log: Send the log… gives it as the game wrote it, zipped with a short summary, by Messages, Mail or AirDrop to whoever helps you; Send to Cartouche sends its start and its end to Cartouche privately, cleaned of the paths of your folders, addresses, names and identifiers, and What Cartouche receives shows exactly what goes first. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Testers' results: on a game's sheet, they now show in your language. Cartouche writes the measured ones itself, with your numbers and dates, and your iPhone translates what testers wrote, once, from iOS 18, with Show the original beside it.
- A game's description, once your iPhone has translated it, shows translated at once the next times you open its sheet, rather than after a few seconds each time.
- Mac: Cartouche Builder 0.6.0 builds each game for your Mac too and plays it there with your iPhone's saves, and its window shows Cartouche's console. Cartouche Builder 0.5.0 and older do not find this version by themselves: download it once from Cartouche's site, and it updates itself again after that.
- Mac: with your Mac paired, a game's sheet now shows its build on that Mac (building, waiting its turn, built, or why it failed), with a button that asks the Mac to build it, as you would on the Mac, and one that stops its build or takes it out of the queue.
- Mac: System has a new page for your Mac's builds: the game building and the queue, Build what is due and Stop all, every game of the Mac, which it follows or not, the builds that failed and why, and its nightly build. The Mac needs the newest version of its app; until then, Cartouche says to update it.
- Saves: Cartouche finds a game's folder in your saves storage by the game's ID, whatever name the Mac gave it, so the saves of a game played on your Mac come back to your iPhone.
- TV mode: if the TV only mirrors your iPhone, the game hides from it, so the touch controls never show there.
- TV mode: while your iPhone's screen is recorded, or shown on a Mac with iPhone Mirroring, the game hides the same way, with a button to show it anyway.
- On an iPad, a game made to be played sideways now stays sideways behind the console instead of turning upright with the iPad, and an iPad held upright asks you to turn it. Games nxnative built since November 4 turn with the iPad. Cartouche also calls your iPad an iPad rather than an iPhone. Never tried on a real iPad yet.
- Signing in to Apple is more reliable: when Apple's sign-in server answers "too many requests", Cartouche now sends the request again, a second apart, up to 10 times, as the Cartouche Installer does, instead of stopping and making you wait 15 minutes.
- When signing in stops because Cartouche could not reach your iPhone through LocalDevVPN, it now says what to do from why: put the pairing file in Cartouche again with the Cartouche Installer, first deleting the pairing the Installer keeps if your iPhone refused it, or restart your iPhone if it did not answer.
- If the built-in SideStore closes while you sign in, Cartouche now says so in your language, with what to do: restart your iPhone, then try again, and install the iOS update offered, if there is one. Until now it showed an English sentence, or the sign-in never ended.
- Put the pairing file in Cartouche again, in the Cartouche Installer, now does what it says: Cartouche uses the new pairing file. Until now it went on with the first one, so replacing a pairing file your iPhone refused did not help. The same goes for a pairing file you give Cartouche yourself.
- If your Cartouche never managed to sign in to Apple, install this version from a computer with the Cartouche Installer, over your copy: your games and saves stay. From now on, System says so itself in a copy that is not set up yet.
- Install with no computer, with your own signing certificate: each release now has a second IPA for a signing app on the iPhone, Cartouche-0.13.0-Own-Certificate.ipa for this one. Sign it there with your signing certificate (.p12) and its profile, open Cartouche and give it that certificate and its password: no Apple ID, no LocalDevVPN, no weekly renewal. Games start in Cartouche's place. System > Setup says whether the signature lacks Increased Memory Limit (about 3 GB without it) or the games' keychain groups, and each new version is offered to download, then sign again. Never tried with a real certificate yet.
- Signing apps: when one on the iPhone signed the IPA made for an Apple ID, signing in cannot work. Cartouche now says so as it opens, and offers the same version's IPA for your own certificate to sign instead, or the Cartouche Installer on a computer. Never tried with a signing app yet.
- Storage: when an SMB server does not sign you in, Cartouche now says why in its own words, as it opens a folder and as Add a shared folder lists the shared folders: the user name or the password refused, a server that does not let guests in, an account locked after too many wrong passwords, or one the server holds back, with what to do, instead of "Logon Failure" or "Unknown error".
- New at the end of System: Reset Cartouche erases what you put into Cartouche, your games with their saves and settings, the storage places you added, the Apple ID you signed in with and Cartouche's settings, then starts it again as just installed, without a computer. The signing certificate and the pairing file stay, so you only sign in again; your storage folders and what they hold stay too.
- Before it erases, Reset Cartouche names the games whose saves are not in your saves folder yet, and can send them there first.
- What's new: after each update, Cartouche now opens on what the new version brings, in your language when its notes are written in it, until you press Continue. System > What's new keeps the notes of the last ten versions.
- Measurements: Cartouche now also sends what renewed it and whether it opened LocalDevVPN first, how many times a sign-in asked Apple again, why it could not reach your iPhone, why a game did not sign whole or start, whether the signature of your own certificate carries Increased Memory Limit and the games' keychain groups, a game started by Siri or from the Home Screen, the memory limit a game in Cartouche's place had at its peak, and a start of Cartouche that never reached the console. Still never your Apple ID, your iPhone's name, your files or the addresses of your storage.
- Cartouche Installer 0.2.2, for Mac and Windows: its second step opens on the choice between your Apple Account and your own certificate, side by side, and Cartouche's IPA for your own certificate is refused with an Apple ID and installed with your own certificate.

A game behind the console shows on your TV, and Cartouche installed with your own certificate opens again.

- TV mode, first version: while a game runs behind the console, plug your iPhone into a TV with a USB-C to HDMI cable, or use AirPlay, and the TV shows the game alone while your iPhone keeps the controls.
- Press Home and the TV shows the game's card, paused, until you resume.
- If your TV shows something else, send System > Report a problem, which now says what the TV did.
